explanation: In C++, operator overloading allows developers to define or customize the behavior of operators (such as <, +, ==) for user-defined types, enabling intuitive syntax and integration with standard algorithms. Specifically, overloading the comparison operator '<' for smart pointers like std::unique_ptr enables comparison based on the pointed-to objects, facilitating sorting and associative container operations involving smart pointers. This enhances code readability and maintains consistency with built-in types while leveraging modern C++ features.
syntax: bool operator<(const std::unique_ptr<T1, D1>& x, const std::unique_ptr<T2, D2>& y);
